claim: Yeast vacuole fusion requires R-SNARE, Q-SNAREs, and HOPS.
source: Yeast vacuole fusion requires R-SNARE, Q-SNAREs, and HOPS.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a foundational requirement for the fusion process.

claim: A HOPS SM-family subunit binds the R- and Qa-SNAREs.
source: A HOPS SM-family subunit binds the R- and Qa-SNAREs.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by prior research cited in the manuscript.

claim: HOPS binds each of the four SNAREs.
source: We now report that HOPS binds each of the four SNAREs.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated through flotation assays in Figure 2.

claim: HOPS catalyzes fusion when the Q-SNAREs are not pre-assembled.
source: HOPS catalyzes fusion when the Q-SNAREs are not pre-assembled, ushering them into a functional complex.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated through fusion assays in Figure 1.

claim: Co-incubation of HOPS, proteoliposomes bearing R-SNARE, and proteoliposomes with any two Q-SNAREs yields a rapid-fusion complex with 3 SNAREs in a trans-assembly.
source: Co-incubation of HOPS, proteoliposomes bearing R-SNARE, and proteoliposomes with any two Q-SNAREs yields a rapid-fusion complex with 3 SNAREs in a trans-assembly.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated through fusion assays in Figures 3, 6, and 8.

claim: The missing Q-SNARE induces sudden fusion when added to the 3-SNARE trans-assembly complex.
source: The missing Q-SNARE then induces sudden fusion.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated through fusion kinetics in Figures 3, 5, and 6.

claim: HOPS can 'template' SNARE complex assembly through SM recognition of R- and Qa-SNAREs.
source: HOPS can 'template' SNARE complex assembly through SM recognition of R- and Qa-SNAREs.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by prior research on SM protein function.

claim: The Qa-SNARE is essential for spontaneous SNARE assembly.
source: Though the Qa-SNARE is essential for spontaneous SNARE assembly, HOPS also assembles a rapid-fusion complex between R- and QbQc-SNARE proteoliposomes in the absence of Qa-SNARE, awaiting Qa for fusion.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated through pulldown assays in Figure 7.

claim: HOPS assembles a rapid-fusion complex between R- and QbQc-SNARE proteoliposomes in the absence of Qa-SNARE.
source: Though the Qa-SNARE is essential for spontaneous SNARE assembly, HOPS also assembles a rapid-fusion complex between R- and QbQc-SNARE proteoliposomes in the absence of Qa-SNARE, awaiting Qa for fusion.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated through fusion assays in Figures 6A and 8.

claim: HOPS-dependent fusion is saturable at low concentrations of each Q-SNARE.
source: HOPS-dependent fusion is saturable at low concentrations of each Q-SNARE, showing binding site functionality.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated through saturation kinetics in Figure 10.

claim: HOPS tethers membranes and recognizes each SNARE, assembling R+Qa or R+QbQc rapid fusion intermediates.
source: HOPS thus tethers membranes and recognizes each SNARE, assembling R+Qa or R+QbQc rapid fusion intermediates.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract, synthesizing the findings from multiple experiments.

claim: Tethering effectors bind Rab family GTPases to hold membranes in apposition.
source: Tethering effectors bind Rab family GTPases to hold membranes in apposition (Baker and Hughson, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claim: SNAREs are grouped by sequence homology into four families: R, Qa, Qb, and Qc.
source: SNAREs are grouped by sequence homology into four families, R, Qa, Qb, and Qc (Fasshauer et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claim: SNARE complexes have one member each of the R, Qa, Qb, and Qc families.
source: SNARE complexes have one member each of the R, Qa, Qb, and Qc families, with their α-helical SNARE domains wrapped together in a coiled coil (Sutton et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claim: SM family proteins have conserved surface grooves to bind the R- and Qa-SNARE domains.
source: Sec1/Munc18 (SM) family proteins (Rizo and Südhof, 2012), which have conserved surface grooves to bind the R- and Qa-SNARE domains (Baker et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: Disassembly of post-fusion cis-SNARE complexes is catalyzed by the ATP-driven chaperone Sec18/NSF, stimulated by its co-chaperone Sec17/αSNAP.
source: Disassembly of the post-fusion cis-SNARE complexes is catalyzed by the ATP-driven chaperone Sec18/NSF, stimulated by its co-chaperone Sec17/αSNAP (Weber et al., 1998; White et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: Sec17 and Sec18 function earlier in the fusion process, stimulating the fusion of docked membranes.
source: Sec17 and Sec18 also function earlier, stimulating the fusion of docked membranes (Song et al., 2017; Zick et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: Fusion requires acidic lipids and phosphoinositides to promote the binding of peripheral membrane fusion proteins.
source: Fusion also requires acidic lipids and phosphoinositides to promote the binding of peripheral membrane fusion proteins (Cheever et al., 2001; Mima and Wickner, 2009; Orr et al., 2015)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: Fusion requires fatty acyl fluidity to enable the bilayer rearrangements essential for fusion.
source: and fatty acyl fluidity (Zick and Wickner, 2016) and nonbilayer-prone lipids (Zick et al., 2014) to enable the bilayer rearrangements which are essential for fusion.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: Vacuoles undergo constant fission and fusion, regulated by growth medium osmolarity.
source: Vacuoles undergo constant fission and fusion, regulated by growth medium osmolarity.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as background on vacuole biology.

claim: Mutations which block fusion allow continued fission, resulting in a visibly altered vacuole morphology.
source: Mutations which block fusion allow continued fission, resulting in a visibly altered vacuole morphology which allowed selection of vam mutants in fusion (Wada et al., 1992).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claim: The VAM genes encode proteins unique to vacuole fusion including the Rab GTPase Ypt7, the 6 subunits of HOPS, and the Qa and Qc SNAREs.
source: The VAM genes encode proteins which are unique to vacuole fusion: the Rab GTPase Ypt7, the 6 subunits of the HOPS (homotypic fusion and vacuole protein sorting) tethering and SM complex (Nakamura et al., 1997; Seals et al., 2000; Wurmser et al., 2000), and the Qa, and Qc SNAREs of this organelle (hereafter referred to as Qa and Qc).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: The R-SNARE Nyv1 was found later than the VAM genes.
source: The R-SNARE Nyv1 was found later (Nichols et al., 1997)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claim: The Qb SNARE Vti1, Sec17, and Sec18 are required in the exocytic pathway and were not identified in the vam screen since their loss is lethal.
source: and other vacuole fusion proteins such as the Qb SNARE Vti1, Sec17, and Sec18 are required in the exocytic pathway and were not identified in the vam screen since their loss is lethal.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an explanation for why certain proteins were not identified in the vam screen.

claim: Vacuole fusion has been studied in vivo, in vitro with the purified organelle, and as reconstituted with proteoliposomes bearing all-purified components.
source: Vacuole fusion has been extensively studied in vivo, in vitro with the purified organelle, and as reconstituted with proteoliposomes bearing all-purified components (Mima et al., 2008; Zick and Wickner, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: The 'priming' stage of vacuole fusion precedes organelle association and entails phosphoinositide synthesis and Sec17- and Sec18-dependent cis-SNARE complex disassembly.
source: The 'priming' stage of vacuole fusion, which precedes organelle association, entails phosphoinositide synthesis (Mayer et al., 2000) and Sec17- and Sec18- dependent cis-SNARE complex disassembly (Mayer et al., 1996).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: Priming is a prerequisite for tethering.
source: Priming is a prerequisite for tethering (Mayer and Wickner, 1997)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claim: Tethering is largely mediated by the affinities of two HOPS subunits (Vps39 and Vps41) for the Rab Ypt7 on each vacuole membrane.
source: which is largely mediated by the affinities of two of the HOPS subunits (Vps39 and Vps41) for the Rab Ypt7 on each vacuole membrane (Brett et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claim: Vacuole fusion differs from synaptic fusion in that vesicle tethering at the active zone of the plasma membrane precedes synaptic priming in synaptic fusion.
source: Vacuole fusion differs in this regard from synaptic fusion, where vesicle tethering at the active zone of the plasma membrane precedes synaptic priming, which assembles SNARE into a release-ready state (Südhof, 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claim: Vacuoles have a 'back-up' tethering system through the affinity of the PX domain of the Qc SNARE for PtdIns3P in trans.
source: Vacuoles also have a 'back-up' tethering system through the affinity of the PX domain of the Qc SNARE for PtdIns3P in trans (Zick and Wickner, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claim: The Vps33 SM-family subunit of HOPS can catalyze the productive association of the R SNARE domain with the Qa SNARE domain, initiating the formation of a 4-SNARE complex.
source: The Vps33 SM-family subunit of HOPS can catalyze the productive association of the R SNARE domain with the Qa SNARE domain, initiating the formation of a 4-SNARE complex (Baker et al., 2015; Jiao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: Fusion can be supported by HOPS and SNAREs alone, but is further accelerated by Sec17 and Sec18p without requiring ATP hydrolysis.
source: Fusion can be supported by HOPS and SNAREs alone, but is further accelerated by Sec17 and Sec18p without requiring ATP hydrolysis (Song et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claim: Fusion proteins and lipids show interdependent co-enrichment on docked vacuoles at a ring-shaped microdomain surrounding the directly apposed bilayers.
source: These fusion proteins and lipids show interdependent co-enrichment on docked vacuoles at a ring-shaped microdomain surrounding the directly apposed bilayers (Wang et al., 2002; Fratti et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: HOPS binds the inherently water-soluble Qc SNARE by the affinity of the Vps16 and Vps18 HOPS subunits for the PX region of Qc that is N-terminal to its SNARE domain.
source: HOPS binds the inherently water-soluble Qc SNARE by the affinity of the Vps16 and Vps18 HOPS subunits (Krämer and Ungermann, 2011) for the PX region of Qc that is N-terminal to its SNARE domain (Stroupe et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: Direct affinity of HOPS for Qb has not been reported.
source: Direct affinity of HOPS for Qb has not been reported.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a gap in prior knowledge.

claim: Proteoliposomes bearing Ypt7 and the R-SNARE underwent HOPS-dependent assembly of all the Q-SNAREs, including Qb, into a 4-SNARE complex.
source: In chemically defined subreactions of fusion, proteoliposomes bearing Ypt7 and the R-SNARE underwent HOPS-dependent assembly of all the Q-SNAREs, including Qb, into a 4-SNARE complex (Orr et al., 2017)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claim: Vps33 protein was shown by single-molecule force spectroscopy to catalyze 4-SNARE assembly.
source: and Vps33 protein was shown by single-molecule force spectroscopy to catalyze 4-SNARE assembly (Jiao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claim: Several Sec17/αSNAP molecules can bind along the length of a 4-SNARE complex.
source: Once a 4-SNARE complex has assembled, several Sec17/αSNAP molecules can bind along its length (Zhao et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claim: The N-terminal apolar loop of SNARE-bound Sec17 has direct affinity for the lipid bilayer.
source: The N-terminal apolar loop of SNARE-bound Sec17 has direct affinity for the lipid bilayer (Zick et al., 2015)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claim: The membrane-distal C-terminus of Sec17 binds Sec18/NSF.
source: while the membrane-distal C-terminus binds Sec18/NSF (Marz et al., 2003; Winter et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: HOPS has direct affinity for phosphoinositides such as PtdIns3P.
source: HOPS also has direct affinity for phosphoinositides such as PtdIns3P (Stroupe et al., 2006)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claim: HOPS has direct affinity for acidic lipids.
source: and for acidic lipids (Karunakaran and Wickner, 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claim: Either HOPS or GST-PX tethering suffices for fusion when proteoliposomes bearing Ypt7 and R-SNARE are mixed with proteoliposomes bearing Ypt7 and the 3 Q-SNAREs.
source: Proteoliposomes bearing Ypt7 and R-SNARE with lumenally entrapped biotinylated phycoerythrin were mixed with proteoliposomes bearing Ypt7 and the 3 Q-SNAREs with entrapped Cy5-streptavidin. These mixed proteoliposomes were incubated without tethering agent, with HOPS, or with GST-PX. Either tethering agent sufficed for fusion, which was detected by the FRET from the mixing of the lumenal dyes (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Tethering is required for productive association of the three pre-assembled Q-SNAREs and the R-SNARE into functional trans-SNARE complex.
source: Although tethering is required, this shows that productive association of the three pre-assembled Q-SNAREs and the R-SNARE into functional trans-SNARE complex does not require catalysis by the Vps33 SM-protein subunit of HOPS
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on the fusion assays in Figure 1A and 1B.

claim: Productive association of the three pre-assembled Q-SNAREs and the R-SNARE into functional trans-SNARE complex does not require catalysis by the Vps33 SM-protein subunit of HOPS.
source: Although tethering is required, this shows that productive association of the three pre-assembled Q-SNAREs and the R-SNARE into functional trans-SNARE complex does not require catalysis by the Vps33 SM-protein subunit of HOPS, consistent with earlier findings that deletion within the R and Qa SNARE recognition domains of the Vps33 subunit of HOPS still permits fusion between R- and QaQbQc-SNARE proteoliposomes (Baker et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to prior work and supported by data in Figure 1A and 1B.

claim: GST-PX does not suffice for fusion when one fusion partner bears only two Q-SNAREs and the third Q-SNARE is added in soluble form.
source: In contrast, GST-PX does not suffice when one fusion partner bears only two Q-SNAREs and the third Q-SNARE is added in soluble form, but HOPS supports such fusion (Figure 1C–E)
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figures 1C-E.

claim: HOPS supports fusion when one fusion partner bears only two Q-SNAREs and the third Q-SNARE is added in soluble form.
source: In contrast, GST-PX does not suffice when one fusion partner bears only two Q-SNAREs and the third Q-SNARE is added in soluble form, but HOPS supports such fusion (Figure 1C–E), suggesting that HOPS helps recruit each Q-SNARE.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figures 1C-E.

claim: HOPS helps recruit each Q-SNARE.
source: In contrast, GST-PX does not suffice when one fusion partner bears only two Q-SNAREs and the third Q-SNARE is added in soluble form, but HOPS supports such fusion (Figure 1C–E), suggesting that HOPS helps recruit each Q-SNARE.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an inference from the data in Figures 1C-E.

claim: The synthetic tether GST-PX supports detectable fusion of R- and QaQb-proteoliposomes with added Qc, but only very slowly and after a 10 min lag.
source: The full kinetic time course shows that the synthetic tether GST-PX did support detectable fusion of R- and QaQb- proteoliposomes with added Qc, but only very slowly and after a 10 min lag (Figure 1E, red curve, and Figure 1—figure supplement 2, curve a).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The lag in fusion with GST-PX was eliminated and the fusion rate enhanced by a 30 min preincubation of the QaQb-SNARE proteoliposomes with Qc-SNARE prior to addition of the GST-PX tether.
source: This lag was eliminated and the fusion rate enhanced by a 30 min preincubation of the QaQb-SNARE proteoliposomes with Qc-SNARE prior to addition of the GST-PX tether (Figure 1—figure supplement 2, curves a vs. c and g)
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: There is a capacity for slow spontaneous assembly of stable 3Q-SNARE complex from QaQb-proteoliposomes and Qc.
source: revealing a capacity for slow spontaneous assembly of stable 3Q-SNARE complex from QaQb-proteoliposomes and Qc (curve g).
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an inference from the data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Spontaneous assembly of stable 3Q-SNARE complex was not seen with GST-PX and 2Q-SNARE proteoliposomes lacking Qa or Qb and supplemented with sQa or sQb, respectively.
source: This was not seen with GST-PX and 2Q-SNARE proteoliposomes lacking Qa or Qb and supplemented with sQa or sQb, respectively (Figure 1C and D), suggesting that these assembly events are kinetically too slow and/or thermodynamically unfavorable.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figures 1C and 1D.

claim: Preincubation of Ypt7/3Q- and Ypt7/R-proteoliposomes with sR for 30 min prior to HOPS addition blocks their fusion.
source: for example, preincubation of Ypt7/3Q- and Ypt7/R-proteoliposomes with sR for 30 min prior to HOPS addition blocks their fusion (Zick and Wickner, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to prior work.

claim: There was complete fusion inhibition when QaQb-proteoliposomes were preincubated with both sR and Qc for 30 min prior to HOPS addition.
source: However, there was complete fusion inhibition when QaQb-proteoliposomes were preincubated with both sR and Qc for 30 min prior to HOPS addition (C, curve a), suggesting sRQaQbQc assembly.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 3C.

claim: Soluble Qa and soluble Qb do not spontaneously enter into complex with the other Q-SNAREs prior to HOPS addition.
source: The contrast between the full inhibition by sR when preincubated with Qc and QaQb proteoliposomes (Figure 1—figure supplement 3, C, curve a) and the lack of inhibition enhancement when either soluble Qa or soluble Qb is preincubated with sR and QbQctm or QaQctm proteoliposomes, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A and B, curve a), is another indication that soluble Qa and Qb do not spontaneously enter into complex with the other Q-SNAREs prior to HOPS addition.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an inference from the data in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: HOPS is required for any one of the Q-SNAREs to assemble rapidly with the others into functional SNARE complex for fusion.
source: In sum, HOPS is required for any one of the Q-SNAREs to assemble rapidly with the others into functional SNARE complex for fusion, though a very slow spontaneous assembly of Qc can occur in the absence of HOPS.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a summary of the findings from Figures 1 and 1—figure supplements.

claim: A very slow spontaneous assembly of Qc can occur in the absence of HOPS.
source: In sum, HOPS is required for any one of the Q-SNAREs to assemble rapidly with the others into functional SNARE complex for fusion, though a very slow spontaneous assembly of Qc can occur in the absence of HOPS.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a summary of the findings from Figures 1 and 1—figure supplements.

claim: HOPS has direct affinity for the PX domain of the Qc SNARE through the HOPS Vps16 and Vps18 subunits.
source: Prior studies have shown that HOPS has direct affinity for the PX domain of the Qc SNARE (Stroupe et al., 2006) through the HOPS Vps16 and Vps18 subunits (Krämer and Ungermann, 2011)
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations to prior work.

claim: HOPS has direct affinity for the R- and Qa-SNARE domains through its Vps33 SM-family subunit.
source: and for the R- and Qa-SNARE domains through its Vps33 SM-family subunit (Baker et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to prior work.

claim: HOPS bound to each of the 4 SNAREs in flotation assays.
source: Although HOPS was not recovered with protein-free liposomes (Figure 2, lane 1; also Figure 2—figure supplement 1), HOPS bound to each of the 4 SNAREs (lanes 2–5) or their complex (lane 6).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 2.

claim: HOPS may bind better to individual SNAREs than to the SNARE complex.
source: There are several possible reasons why HOPS may bind better to individual SNAREs than to the SNARE complex.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an observation from Figure 2.

claim: The large apolar surfaces of the R- and Qa-SNARE domains can bind into grooves on the Vps33 surface.
source: Though the large apolar surfaces of the R- and Qa-SNARE domains can bind into grooves on the Vps33 surface (Baker et al., 2015), these same surfaces are oriented into the center of the 4-helical SNARE complex (Sutton et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations to prior work.

claim: The apolar surfaces of R- and Qa-SNARE domains are oriented into the center of the 4-helical SNARE complex.
source: Though the large apolar surfaces of the R- and Qa-SNARE domains can bind into grooves on the Vps33 surface (Baker et al., 2015), these same surfaces are oriented into the center of the 4-helical SNARE complex (Sutton et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to prior work.

claim: The orientation of apolar surfaces into the center of the 4-helical SNARE complex may shield these surfaces and thereby attenuate their contribution to HOPS binding the 4-SNARE complex.
source: This may shield these apolar surfaces and thereby attenuate their contribution to HOPS binding the 4-SNARE complex.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a speculation about why HOPS may bind better to individual SNAREs.

claim: HOPS binds to Qc through the Qc N-domain.
source: Furthermore, HOPS binds to Qc through the Qc N-domain (Stroupe et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to prior work.

claim: The interactions among the SNARE N-domains in a 4-SNARE complex may modulate the contribution of the Qc N-domain to binding the SNARE complex to HOPS.
source: The interactions among the SNARE N-domains in a 4-SNARE complex may modulate the contribution of the Qc N-domain to binding the SNARE complex to HOPS.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a speculation about why HOPS may bind better to individual SNAREs.

claim: Tethering per se will support functional trans-SNARE formation between R- and Q-SNARE proteoliposomes if the 3 Q-SNAREs are preassembled.
source: Tethering per se will support functional trans-SNARE formation between R- and Q-SNARE proteoliposomes if the 3 Q-SNAREs are preassembled (Song and Wickner, 2019)
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to prior work.

claim: After 30 min of incubation of mixed proteoliposomes with HOPS alone, the addition of Qc triggered very rapid fusion.
source: After 30 min of incubation of mixed proteoliposomes with HOPS alone, the addition of Qc (red curve e) triggered very rapid fusion which was not seen without Qc (curve c), showing that a highly active fusion intermediate had accumulated.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 3A.

claim: A highly active fusion intermediate accumulates when mixed proteoliposomes are incubated with HOPS alone for 30 min.
source: After 30 min of incubation of mixed proteoliposomes with HOPS alone, the addition of Qc (red curve e) triggered very rapid fusion which was not seen without Qc (curve c), showing that a highly active fusion intermediate had accumulated.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an inference from the data in Figure 3A.

claim: HOPS promoted substantial trans complex assembly between R and Qa SNAREs in the absence of Qc while fusion remained blocked.
source: While there was background association of the R and Qa SNAREs in incubations without HOPS or Qc (lane a) and maximal association with both HOPS and Qc (lane d), HOPS promoted substantial trans complex assembly between R and Qa SNAREs in the absence of Qc (lane c) while fusion remained blocked (Figure 3A, curve c).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figures 3B and 3C.

claim: The addition of Qc at 30 min triggered rapid fusion with only a modest increase in trans complex.
source: The addition of Qc at 30 min triggered rapid fusion (Figure 3A, red curve e) with only a modest increase in trans complex (Figure 3C,e vs c).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figures 3A and 3C.

claim: HOPS forms an assembly which includes the R- and Qa-SNAREs in trans.
source: HOPS thus forms an assembly which includes the R- and Qa-SNAREs in trans, whether directly with each other in coiled coils 3-SNARE bundles or with the R- and the two Q- SNAREs associated with common HOPS molecules or by some combination of these associations.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the data in Figure 3.

claim: The HOPS-dependent fusion intermediate between Ypt7/R and Ypt7/QaQb proteoliposomes is compatible with Sec17, Sec18, and ATP.
source: Is the rapid-fusion intermediate which HOPS forms with Ypt7/R and Ypt7/QaQb proteoliposomes compatible with Sec17, Sec18, and ATP? Ypt7/R- and Ypt7/QaQb-SNARE proteoliposomes fuse when incubated with HOPS and Qc (Figure 4A, solid black curve a; also Figure 4—figure supplement 1). When Qc is withheld, there is no fusion, but upon its addition there is rapid fusion (dotted black curve d). Sec17/Sec18/ATP does not inhibit fusion, whether added from the start of incubations with HOPS and Qc (solid blue curve b) or after 25 min (solid red curve c).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 4A.

claim: The R- and Qa-SNAREs alone will suffice for a HOPS-dependent assembly of a rapid-fusion intermediate.
source: Thus, the R- and Qa-SNAREs alone will suffice for a HOPS-dependent assembly of a rapid-fusion intermediate.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the data in Figure 5A.

claim: Wild-type Qc has a labile association with the HOPS:R:Qa rapid-fusion machinery, taking a minute for full dissociation of Qc and capture by Qc-3Δ.
source: Had there been no association between wild-type Qc and the HOPS:R:Qa rapid-fusion machinery, the same fusion would have been seen in d-i, which each had the same 40-fold excess of Qc-3Δ to Qc at the time of sQb addition. The data indicate a labile association of wild-type Qc with the HOPS:R:Qa rapid-fusion machinery, taking a minute for full dissociation of Qc and capture by Qc-3Δ.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an inference from the data in Figure 5B.

claim: For each Q-SNARE, the fusion was distinctly more rapid when the soluble Q-SNARE was added after 30 min than when it had been added from the start.
source: For each Q-SNARE, the fusion was distinctly more rapid when the soluble Q-SNARE was added after 30 min (Figure 6A–C, red curve b; see Figure 6—figure supplement 1) than when it had been added from the start (curve a), indicating that HOPS allowed the accumulation of fusion-competent intermediates which included either R and QaQb, R and QaQctm, or R and QbQctm, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figures 6A-C.

claim: HOPS allowed the accumulation of fusion-competent intermediates which included either R and QaQb, R and QaQctm, or R and QbQctm.
source: For each Q-SNARE, the fusion was distinctly more rapid when the soluble Q-SNARE was added after 30 min (Figure 6A–C, red curve b; see Figure 6—figure supplement 1) than when it had been added from the start (curve a), indicating that HOPS allowed the accumulation of fusion-competent intermediates which included either R and QaQb, R and QaQctm, or R and QbQctm, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an inference from the data in Figures 6A-C.

claim: The formation of the rapid-fusion state required the presence of HOPS during the preincubation.
source: The formation of the rapid-fusion state required the presence of HOPS during the preincubation (compare curve b to curves c, d).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figures 6A-C.

claim: The action of HOPS is not merely due to its tethering function, as the synthetic tether GST-PX does not support fusion at all unless the three Q-SNAREs have been pre-assembled.
source: The action of HOPS is not merely due to its tethering function, as the synthetic tether GST-PX does not support fusion at all unless the three Q-SNAREs have been pre-assembled (Figure 1).
